title: The Story of Walking Upright is Written in the Bones of Our Ancestors - Nautilus
gist: A Science Advances study used CT scans to compare limb-bone thickness in the 3.7-million-year-old Australopithecus 'Little Foot' with Homo specimens about 1.8 million years old, using bone thickness as a proxy for activity to clarify how often early hominins walked upright.

insights.claim: Bipedalism is a hallmark of the human genus, but it is unclear how often Australopithecus, one of our earliest ancestors, chose to walk upright even though it was able to.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: An open scientific question with no direct market angle.
